name: Variable Player Powers
description: A mechanic where each player, or the faction/role they control, starts with unique abilities, strengths, weaknesses, or different starting conditions that significantly distinguish their gameplay from others. These powers are typically fixed for the duration of the game and often guide a player's strategy.

parameters.name: Source of Powers
parameters.description: How are player powers determined (e.g., chosen from a pool, assigned randomly, tied to a specific faction/character selected by the player).

parameters.name: Nature of Powers
parameters.description: What aspects of the game do the powers affect (e.g., resource generation, movement, combat, scoring, special actions, rule exceptions).

parameters.name: Symmetry vs. Asymmetry Level
parameters.description: How different are the powers? Are they minor variations or do they lead to completely different playstyles and objectives?
parameters.default_value: Significant asymmetry leading to different playstyles

parameters.name: Power Evolution
parameters.description: Can player powers change or be upgraded during the game, or are they static from the start?

examples_in_games.specific_implementation_notes: The classic example; each alien race has a unique, often game-breaking, power that defines its playstyle.
Each faction plays an entirely different game with unique rules, actions, and victory conditions, driven by their variable powers.
Each faction has unique abilities, starting resources, and costs/benefits for certain actions, guiding their expansion and development.
Each faction has a unique faction ability and a different starting position and set of starting resources/popularity/power. Player mats also have slightly different action costs/benefits.
Each character class has a unique deck of ability cards and perks, leading to very different tactical roles in combat scenarios.

notes_on_combination_modification: Variable player powers greatly enhance replayability and allow players to explore different strategies. Balancing these asymmetric powers is a key design challenge.
